jobs.occupation: Junior Consultant - Europe Central Inhouse Consulting
jobs.description:
At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

The opportunity: your next adventure awaits

Would you like to gain hands-on consulting experience while helping shape and transform a large international organization from within?

Our Europe Central Inhouse Consulting team is growing, and we are looking for a Junior Consultant to join us in January 2027. You will work on real projects with stakeholders across Europe Central and gain insight into the priorities and operations of one of the world’s leading professional services organization.

We act as an internal consulting partner to EY leadership, Functions and Service Lines across 33 countries. We help solve complex business challenges, translate strategic priorities into practical solutions and deliver change with lasting impact.

We are a small, collaborative team with a hands-on, pragmatic approach. We value constructive problem-solvers who take ownership, create momentum and turn ideas into results. You will receive coaching and mentoring and work closely with experienced consultants, leaders and colleagues across the organization.

The role averages 15-20 hours per week, with flexibility during exam periods.

What you will work on

• 
Support consulting projects from problem definition and planning through analysis, recommendations and implementation

• 
Conduct research and analyze data to identify patterns, gaps and insights

• 
Turn complex information into clear presentations, dashboards and decision material

• 
Maintain project plans and track milestones, actions, risks and dependencies

• 
Help prepare and facilitate meetings and workshops, including documenting decisions and follow-up actions

• 
Take ownership of selected analyses and deliverables, with increasing responsibility as you grow in the role

What we look for

• 
You are curious, structured and eager to learn how consulting works in practice. You enjoy bringing clarity to complex information, ask thoughtful questions and take ownership of your work.

• 
A positive, proactive and can-do attitude

• 
Strong analytical and structured problem-solving skills

• 
A collaborative mindset and an interest in working across cultures and perspectives

• 
Clear written and verbal communication skills

• 
Attention to detail and the ability to manage several tasks and deadlines

Qualifications

• 
You are studying for a relevant degree, such as Business Administration, Economics or a related field, and are at least in the fifth semester of your bachelor’s degree

• 
You are fluent in written and spoken English

• 
You have experience with Microsoft 365 product suite

What’s in it for you

• 
Hands-on experience on high-impact projects across Europe Central, with real responsibility and the opportunity to develop your consulting toolbox

• 
Close collaboration with experienced consultants and senior stakeholders

• 
A counselor and buddy to support your onboarding and development

• 
A supportive, international team where we share knowledge, challenge each other constructively and help each other succeed

• 
A hybrid working model based in Copenhagen, with flexibility around your studies

What you can expect

If this sounds like a team and a challenge you would enjoy, we would love to hear from you. Application deadline: 14 December 2026

The steps in our recruitment process are as follows:

• 
Application: Upload a cover letter, your CV along with your most recent grade transcript before the application deadline.

• 
Assessment: After submitting your application, you will receive a link to our assessment within a few days. The assessment takes approximately 20 minutes to complete.

• 
Interview: Selected candidates will be invited for interviews at our office at Marmormolen.

As we review applications continuously, we recommend applying promptly, as the position may be filled before the deadline.

If you have any questions, please contact Georgios Karsiotis at +45 2529 4800.

Are you ready to shape your future with confidence? Apply today.

jobs.description:

Can you be the client advisor handling the discipline lead for an electrical project or a design lead that collaborates with the bigger project team? Then become one of COWI's specialists within data center and industry!

Turn challenges into sustainable solutions

We are looking for a client advisor or specialist to join our team in the Electrical Industrial Engineering discipline in Lyngby. You will be involved in all aspects of client advisory and within the electrical engineering, we are a team of over 60 electrical professionals within the Building and Industry division. Our core services include detailed electrical design and project execution, with a focus on industrial power systems, Data Center design, Data Centre infrastructure and buildings, emergency power supply in low-voltage installations, technical due diligence, commissioning, construction management, supervision, energy screening, and other technical services related to electrical systems.

We take a holistic approach to our projects, aiming to create maximum value for our clients, who include leading Danish and international companies in the industrial and data center sectors. This role offers the opportunity to contribute to our professional development and future growth, while collaborating across Denmark and with our Engineering Design Centres in Lithuania and India, where daily teamwork is centered around delivering the highest quality solutions.

• To define design, planning, specification, follow-up, tender and procurement, supervision, and quality assurance for projects where you are the client advisor and discipline lead.

• To manage and execute tasks related to low- and medium-voltage electrical systems, emergency power systems, and data, telecommunication, and security systems.

• To co-create projects together with colleagues and customers.

• To ensure coordination across disciplines, including BIM, architects, contractors, and other partners, throughout all construction phases, while ensuring constructability.

• To contribute to the development of our professional electrical engineering environment in collaboration with our professional forum.

• To work on projects within Datacenters, Pharma, Hospitals, Transport Hubs, Industrial Buildings, and Power-to-X.

**

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

• Experience with BIM and Novapoints Civil 3D design.

• You are structured and thrive in an environment with shifting priorities, where a flexible responsiveness to customer needs is necessary to obtain success.

• The ability to inspire others and be inspired by the ideas of colleagues and partners.

**At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers. Budget & Reporting Manager

Introduction

Would you like to own budgeting, forecasting and reporting in an ambitious FP&A team?

Scandlines operates ferry routes between Denmark and Germany. FP&A is a finance-oriented Performance Management function, organised with Budget & Reporting, Commercial, Operations and Headquarter functions.

As Budget & Reporting Manager, you will be the one who keeps the processes, the numbers and the reporting together. You will report to the Head of FP&A and play a central role in a small and ambitious team.

Area of responsiblities

You will own the processes and deliverables that the rest of FP&A and the business build on:

• Budget and forecast processes: you run the calendar, templates and deadlines, and hold the business and the controllers to them.

• Rolling forecast: you own the model and ensure that P&L, balance sheet and cash flow are consistent.

• Management report: you own the segment reporting by business area and the KPI pack, and continuously improve and standardise it together with BI.

• Capex reporting: you report and follow up on capex and phase it into the cash forecast.

• You are responsible for budgeting and follow-up on a few areas

• A degree in business or finance, e.g. an MSc in Business Economics, HD or equivalent.

• Several years of experience in FP&A, budgeting or controlling, ideally in a capital-intensive group within transport, infrastructure or energy.

• Experience running budget and forecast processes, ideally rolling and driver-based forecasting.

• A solid understanding of how P&L, balance sheet and cash flow connect, including the phasing of capex.

• Experience developing and standardising management reporting and KPIs.

• Strong Excel and financial modelling skills, and experience with planning and BI tools.

• Fluent Danish and English, written and spoken.

Personal skills

• You thrive on structure and well-defined processes. You own the recurring tasks and make them better every time.

• You are precise and thorough. Your numbers hold up, and you document your work so others can build on it.

• You take initiative and meet deadlines. You report status proactively and act before anyone asks.

• You are not afraid to challenge. You question established habits and numbers, including with executives and your manager.

• You have impact. You can hold budget owners to agreed processes and deadlines.

• You value sparring. You want to develop and use your manager as a sparring partner.

This PhD project is part of a new Independent Research Fund project Smooth Tileable Surfaces. Joining the section for Mathematics at DTU Compute, you will help to develop the mathematical theory of a new class of surfaces in geometry, that are characterized as being decomposable into many copies of a small number of so-called prototiles. 

The subject has links to several areas of mathematics, including differential geometry and topology, graph theory and tiling theory, as well as applications in architecture and fabrication. 

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your focus is to help develop the new subject of smooth tileable surfaces by a) classifying generic subclasses of these surfaces b) establishing an understanding of their relations with graph theory and polyhedral theory, and c) developing methods for geometrically controlled generation of many examples of these surfaces. The overall project also involves collaboration with other team members, working towards the goal of developing not only the mathematical theory of these surfaces, but also algorithms for utilizing them in practical applications in architecture and fabrication.

You must have a background that includes a substantial amount of experience in mathematics, including:

• at least elementary differential geometry, 
• knowledge of, and interest in, some or all of the following subject areas: geometry of surfaces, topology, computational geometry, graph theory, group theory.
A genuine interest in the interplay between theoretical mathematics and applications is also essential.

During the 3 year programme you will:

• Investigate and prove theoretical properties of tileable surfaces
• Develop methods for controlled generation of these surfaces
• Collaborate with other team members on the scientific aspects of the project
• Publish articles in high quality scientific journals
• Present results at scientific conferences
• Contribute to teaching and co-supervision of BsC and MSc students
• Pass approximately 30 ECTS points of relevant coursework
You must have a two-year master's degree in mathematics (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

The period of employment is 3 years. The expected starting date is 1 March 2027 with some flexibility. The position is a full-time position. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information

**Job Description Summary

**The Production Engineer – Calibration & Maintenance is responsible for the calibration, maintenance, and lifecycle management of production, inspection, measurement, and test equipment used in a regulated medical device manufacturing environment.

The role works closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, equipment owners, and external service providers to ensure equipment remains calibrated, maintained, compliant, and available for production.

Responsibilities include day-to-day calibration and preventive maintenance coordination, HxGN EAM administration, calibration assessments, controlled procedures and work instructions, supplier coordination, and equipment compliance.

This is a hands-on Production Engineering role supporting manufacturing operations across scanner/system assembly, mechanical and electrical/electronic assembly, software configuration/loading, packaging and labeling, and testing/final acceptance.

**Job Description

****Roles & Responsibilities

**

• Coordinate the site calibration program, including calibration schedules, call-in activities, equipment status, due dates, and timely completion.

• Coordinate internal and external calibration activities, including equipment preparation, shipment, return, documentation review, and release back to production.

• Ensure new, returned, overdue, failed, or out-of-tolerance equipment is appropriately assessed and controlled before use.

• Act as SME for calibration and maintenance activities in HxGN EAM, maintaining asset records, calibration setups, preventive maintenance schedules, work orders, task plans, and supporting documentation.

• Perform and support calibration assessments, including equipment requirements, criticality, acceptance criteria, calibration methods, frequencies, and maintenance needs.

• Develop and maintain calibration and maintenance procedures, SOPs, and work instructions in collaboration with equipment owners, SMEs, and Quality.

• Coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance activities for production and test equipment while minimizing disruption to manufacturing.

• Support investigations, risk assessments, and product-impact assessments related to overdue, failed, or out-of-tolerance equipment, and provide input to NC/INV/CAPA activities where applicable.

• Coordinate external calibration and maintenance suppliers, including quotations, service activities, documentation, and AGORA purchase orders.

• Support internal and external audits by ensuring calibration and maintenance records are complete, traceable, compliant, and audit-ready.

• Monitor calibration and maintenance performance and drive improvements in equipment compliance, availability, data quality, and execution efficiency.
